entityDescription: ZikaSeal is a Danish company combining satellite-based mosquito risk mapping with innovative hardware to combat mosquito-borne diseases in urban environments. The solution targets invasive species such as Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito), a known vector of the Zika, Dengue, and Chikungunya viruses. ZikaSeal offers municipalities and utility companies a pesticide-free, scalable, and environmentally sustainable method of vector control.

With the foundation of CYCLO GmbH in 1931, Lorenz Braren, the inventor of the unique CYCLO reducer, made a piece of industrial history. The bestowal of a licence on Sumitomo Heavy Industries in 1935 was the commencement of one of the oldest examples of German-Japanese industrial co-operation, which led in 1974 to a share bolding and in 1994 to the total inclusion of CYCLO GmbH into the Sumitomo Corporation.The Sumitomo Group is one of the largest industrial concerns in Japan and is active in widely varied industries. Sumitomo Heavy Industries is the market leader in drive technology in Japan and also one of the largest suppliers in the world.
SM CYCLO ITALY SRL is the Italian subsidiary of Germany's Sumitomo Cyclo Europe, in turn part of Japan's Sumitomo Group, active in distributing Sumitomo Drive Technologies products throughout the country. The Cornaredo (MI) office, thanks to a highly qualified staff, acts as a problem-solver, offering solutions for the world of precision. The Sumitomo Group is active in the most diverse industrial sectors: production automation, plastics and rubber processing, civil engineering, food industry, agriculture, metal processing, textile industry, and many others. 
The main business activities of SM CYCLO ITALY SRL consist of the design, assembly and sale of (i) precision and zero-backlash gearboxes, (ii) gearboxes and gearmotors, and (iii) special gearboxes for centrifugal applications. The Company is controlled by Sumitomo (SHI) Cyclo Drive Germany GmbH, a company that exercises management and coordination activities, is headquartered in Markt Indersdorf (Munich - DE), holds 100% of the share capital, and carries out the manufacturing activities of a large part of the gearboxes sold by SM CYCLO ITALY SRL in the domestic market.

Pannon Business Network (PBN) is a leading applied innovation and ecosystem-building organisation based in Western Hungary, operating at the intersection of industry, research, education, and regional development. PBN acts as a cross-border innovation hub connecting Hungarian, Austrian, German, and wider European ecosystems, with a strong focus on Industry 4.0/5.0, advanced manufacturing, robotics and humanoid systems, AI-enabled solutions, digital twins, circular economy, and health- and age-tech applications. Its mission is to translate emerging technologies into practical, scalable, and market-ready solutions for SMEs, public actors, and industrial partners.
The organisation operates three complementary laboratories, forming an integrated applied innovation environment:
- a Humanoid Test Centre Laboratory, dedicated to human-centric robotics, physical AI, and real-world validation of humanoid and assistive systems;

- am-Lab, advanced manufacturing - embedded in a Teaching and Learning Factory framework, supporting advanced manufacturing, supplier transformation, skills development, and Industry 4.0/5.0 pilot implementations;

- Space Lab, currently under development, focusing on space-related technologies, testing, and cross-sector technology transfer with downstream industrial and dual-use applications.

Together, these labs enable technology validation, experimentation, training, and deployment in real operational contexts, bridging the gap between research excellence and industrial uptake.
PBN is an experienced coordinator and partner in EU-funded programmes (Interreg, Horizon Europe, I3, EIT-related actions), with a strong track record in cross-border cooperation, ecosystem orchestration, and institutional capacity building. It works closely with universities, research institutes, chambers, clusters, municipalities, and industry leaders to strengthen regional competitiveness and resilience.
Strategically, PBN positions itself as a neutral innovation integrator, aligning policy objectives, technological development, workforce skills, and business models. Through this role, it enables regions and organisations to adopt human-centric, sustainable, and future-proof industrial solutions, while actively contributing to Europe’s twin transition and long-term strategic autonomy.

Farmers’ Parliament (ZSA) is the most influential and constructive non-governmental organization of agricultural and horticultural produce producers in Latvia. The ZSA was founded in 1999, uniting 134 strong and far-sighted farms with a common goal – to fight for the interests of Latvian farmers and to strengthen the competitiveness of Latvian farmers. Currently, the union brings together around 800 purposeful members representing all agricultural sectors.
We work to give you a voice, protect your lifestyle in the countryside of Latvia now and in the future. The aim of the organization is to support Latvian agriculture and horticulture by promoting stable and sustainable growth for Latvian farmers!
The main work of the ZSA is representation of interests of Latvian farmers, involvement in the legislative process at the level of national and European Union (EU). We explain and help implement the latest laws, regulations and EU regulations in farms. The union regularly organizes seminars and conferences about the latest and most up-to-date information on the various agricultural sectors.
Our board and members regularly participate in interviews, TV and radio broadcasts, expressing their views on hot topics in the agricultural sector. We also cooperate with other NGOs and institutions.
Our work has paid off – ZSA members in Latvia manage over 662,000 ha of available agricultural land, and each year these areas grow. There are more than 6,000 jobs in the member farms for the local population. So we represent not only our members, but we also protect families that are maintained by our farm workers.
Agriculture is the strongest sector in Latvia and we can be proud of being the leading NGO in this sector!

empiriQa is a high-tech spin-off company emerging from the Single Photon Application Laboratory (SPALab) at the Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, Poland. Structured as a Limited Liability Company (Sp. z o.o.), the company commercializes over 20 years of specialized research and know-how in quantum optics and Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The company bridges the gap between advanced academic research and industrial implementation, specifically addressing the critical security threats posed by future Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQC).
The company’s mission is to secure global data infrastructure against the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat by providing physics-based, unconditionally secure communication solutions. The company operates on a "Full-Stack" model, delivering proprietary hardware and specialized verification services. The core value proposition is built upon three pillars:
1. Quantum Communication Hardware (Upstream & Ground Segment): The company designs and manufactures critical components for the quantum supply chain. This includes proprietary Optical Ground Stations (OGS) for satellite-based QKD and high-performance Quantum Key Generators (Entangled Photon Sources) designed for both terrestrial and space-based applications.
2. Verification & Validation (V&V) Services: A unique auditing capability that distinguishes the company in the European market. The entity provides independent "Quantum-Safe Readiness Audits" and security certifications to ensure that third-party QKD installations are free from implementation flaws and "backdoors". This service leverages methodologies aligned with ETSI and ECSS standards.
3. System Integration and quantum resistance audits: Expertise in integrating quantum layers into existing telecommunications infrastructure for government and defense clients
